findings.title: test_handoff_concurrency uses sleep for synchronization instead of real contention
findings.why: The test spawns 4 threads writing to a locked JSONL in a tight loop (_PER_THREAD=300), but does NOT use a threading.Barrier or any explicit synchronization primitive to force ACTUAL contention. The ThreadPoolExecutor.map call schedules work but does not guarantee overlapping execution — on a single-core or under-loaded system threads may serialize naturally, defeating the test's purpose of detecting torn writes.
findings.recommendation: Add a threading.Barrier(4) before the tight loop in _writer, matching the pattern in test_per_task_env_isolation.py:_run_worker (line 1207). This forces all 4 threads to align their starts, maximizing collision probability and making the test a real concurrency stress test.

findings.title: test_handoff_crash_consistency does not actually interrupt a mid-write
findings.why: The test's docstring says it validates 'crash BETWEEN the handoff write and the JSONL append,' but the test ONLY writes the handoff record via store.write() (which completes atomically) and never emits the corresponding task_complete JSONL event. This simulates the crash-window state but does NOT test that a crash mid-write cannot corrupt the handoff file itself — it only tests resume semantics given a pre-existing asymmetry. A true crash-consistency test would need to interrupt FileHandoffStore.write between the temp write and the replace.
findings.recommendation: Rename the test or adjust its docstring to clarify it validates 'resume honors handoff file without journal event' (the recovery semantics) rather than 'crash during write cannot corrupt handoff file' (atomic write property). Add a separate test that patches pathlib.Path.replace to raise mid-call and asserts the final handoff file is either absent or complete (never partial).

findings.title: test_parallel_k4_under_half_serial_wallclock relies on time.sleep synchronization
findings.why: The parallel wall-clock speedup test uses time.sleep(0.2) as the mock task duration, which is a brittle synchronization primitive. Under CPU pressure or virtualized CI, sleeps can wake late (e.g., 0.25s instead of 0.2s), causing the 4-task parallel run to exceed 0.5x serial time even with perfect scheduling, producing flaky failures. The test also lacks warmup to exclude ThreadPoolExecutor cold-start overhead.
findings.recommendation: Replace time.sleep with a threading.Event-based barrier that the test can trigger precisely, or increase _TASK_SLEEP to 0.5s and the threshold to <0.6x serial to add margin. Add a warmup run to exclude cold-start overhead from measurements. Alternatively, count actual concurrent execution (e.g., a shared counter protected by a lock that tracks max simultaneous active tasks) rather than relying on wall-clock ratios.

findings.title: fake_claude.py FAKE_CLAUDE_NUM_TURNS defaults to 0, masking the pre-change hard-coded 0 bug
findings.why: The fake_claude harness defaults FAKE_CLAUDE_NUM_TURNS to 0, which matches the PRE-change hard-coded turns_consumed=0 in _run_task_subprocess. This means any e2e test that does NOT explicitly set FAKE_CLAUDE_NUM_TURNS will pass against BOTH the old and new code, failing to detect the regression the Stage-0 wiring is supposed to prevent. Only test_e2e_turn_count.py explicitly sets it to 7, so the other e2e tests (isolation_smoke, rerun_happy_path, sha_guard_real_edit) are vacuous w.r.t. turn counting.
findings.recommendation: Change the default to a non-zero sentinel (e.g., 3) so tests that forget to set FAKE_CLAUDE_NUM_TURNS still exercise the turn-parsing path and would fail against the old hard-coded 0. Alternatively, add an assertion in the fake_claude harness that fails if FAKE_CLAUDE_NUM_TURNS is unset during a per-task run, forcing every e2e test to declare its expected turn count explicitly.

findings.title: test_handoff_backward_compat does not verify zero extra daemon threads claim
findings.why: The test asserts 'zero extra daemon threads (legacy thread-count parity)' but allows post_threads to be baseline+1 (<=), not baseline. The docstring claims the gate is 'zero extra daemon threads' but the assertion permits one extra. Either the assertion is wrong (should be == baseline) or the docstring/comment is misleading. The time.sleep(0.1) before checking post_threads is also insufficient to join all worker threads if K>1; ThreadPoolExecutor.__exit__ blocks until workers finish, but other daemon threads may still be terminating.
findings.recommendation: If the test truly requires zero new threads, change the assertion to post_threads == baseline_threads. If +1 is acceptable (e.g., for a logger background thread), update the docstring to say 'at most one extra thread.' Add a longer sleep (e.g., 0.5s) or explicitly join all known background threads before counting.

findings.title: test_in_flight_dependency_dependents_wait_on_resume does not verify dependency ordering
findings.why: The test asserts T01.01 launched before T01.02 (index order), which proves serial execution but does NOT prove the scheduler honored the dependency edge during parallel execution. The test uses task_parallelism=4 but the two-task scenario always serializes (wave 1: T01.01 alone, wave 2: T01.02). To test the 'in-flight dependency prevents premature launch' claim, the test needs >=3 tasks: an in-flight dependency D, its dependent X, and an independent task Y. If D has no handoff record, the scheduler must launch D before X but can launch Y concurrently with D. The current test cannot distinguish parallel-safe dependency ordering from accidental serialization.
findings.recommendation: Expand the test to 4 tasks: T01.01 (in-flight dep), T01.02 (dependent of T01.01), T01.03 (independent), T01.04 (dependent of T01.03). Assert T01.01 < T01.02 and T01.03 < T01.04 in launch order, but allow T01.01 and T01.03 to launch concurrently (via timestamps or a shared launch log with sub-second resolution). This proves the scheduler respects dependency edges under K>1 without over-serializing.

findings.title: test_shared_settings_dir_contention_is_detectable downgrades to xfail on no contention
findings.evidence:
pytest.xfail(
    "no torn read forced on this runner; all workers shared one "
    "CLAUDE_SETTINGS_DIR — harness would catch corruption absent isolation"
)
findings.why: The negative control uses pytest.xfail when it cannot force a race (all workers exit 0), which makes the test non-blocking but also non-verifying. On a single-core or lightly-loaded runner, the test will xfail every time, providing zero signal about whether the harness can actually detect corruption. This is safer than a flaky fail but means the test suite cannot assert 'the negative control works on this platform.'
findings.recommendation: Add pytest.mark.skip with a platform/concurrency check (e.g., skip if multiprocessing.cpu_count() == 1), or increase the worker loop iteration count to force a collision even under serialization (e.g., 1000 iterations instead of 60). Alternatively, log the xfail reason to CI telemetry so teams know which runners are not exercising the negative control.

findings.title: test_executor backward_compat test for ThreadPoolExecutor now allows the import
findings.why: The backward-compat test was updated from 'no threading import' to 'no leaked daemon threads,' but the new check only asserts ThreadPoolExecutor is context-managed (via 'with'). This is weaker than the original invariant and could miss a leak if the context manager is entered but never exited (e.g., due to an exception before the with block closes). The test also does NOT verify that raw Thread() spawns are absent (only checks 'Thread(' and 'daemon=True' strings), which could be bypassed by 'Thread (' with a space or importing Thread with an alias.
findings.recommendation: Strengthen the string checks to cover whitespace variants ('Thread\s*\(') and common aliases ('from threading import Thread as T'). Add a runtime test that spawns execute_phase_tasks, counts threading.active_count() before and after, and asserts no increase (matching the handoff_backward_compat test pattern). This catches actual leaks the static string check misses.

findings.title: test_write_preliminary_result patches os.open but does not verify the sentinel path
findings.why: The test patches os.open to raise OSError, which exercises the telemetry branch and verifies return_val is False and a WARNING is logged. But it does NOT assert that the sentinel file was NOT created (the whole point of the O_EXCL atomic write). A buggy implementation that writes the sentinel via Path.write_text (which does NOT use os.open) would still pass this test, even though it bypassed the RC.4 O_EXCL guard.
findings.recommendation: After the patched call, assert the sentinel file does not exist: assert not config.preliminary_result_sentinel(phase).exists(). Also add a positive test that verifies a SUCCESSFUL _write_preliminary_result call DOES create the sentinel via O_EXCL (e.g., by asserting the file exists and attempting a second write, which should fail with FileExistsError).

cross_cutting_observations.title: No coverage for TurnLedger.try_launch atomicity under concurrent K>1 execution
cross_cutting_observations.why: TurnLedger.try_launch (models.py:956) is the TOCTOU fix for Stage 3 bounded parallelism — it atomically checks can_launch() and debits under a lock. But NO test spawns >=2 real concurrent workers (threading.Thread or ThreadPoolExecutor) that both call try_launch on a shared ledger with EXACTLY minimum_allocation budget remaining, forcing one to succeed and one to fail. The existing parallel tests (test_handoff_performance.py) use a large budget so both workers pass, and the concurrency test (test_handoff_concurrency.py) only tests JSONL locking, not ledger locking. Without a contention test, a regression that drops the lock or reverts to separate can_launch/debit calls would go undetected.
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Add tests/sprint/test_turn_ledger_concurrency.py with a test that spawns 2 workers via threading.Barrier, both calling try_launch on a ledger with initial_budget=5 (exactly 1 allocation). Assert exactly one worker returns True and one returns False, and final ledger.consumed==5 (not 10, which would indicate double-debit). Run this 100 times in a loop to catch non-deterministic races.

cross_cutting_observations.title: No tests verify SHA-guard actually compares file hashes before and after
cross_cutting_observations.why: test_e2e_sha_guard_real_edit.py has two tests: test_no_false_trip_engine_provenance_write (negative) and test_detects_operator_edit_blocks_merge (positive). The negative test verifies a normal rerun does NOT trip the guard, and the positive test verifies an operator edit DOES trip it. But neither test asserts the SHA-guard MECHANISM works — i.e., that the guard compares the SHA of the file at rerun start vs. the SHA at original completion. A buggy implementation that always passes or always fails would satisfy these tests as long as the operator-edit path trips. The tests also do not verify the SHA is stored in the handoff record or phase-result JSON.
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Add a unit test for the SHA comparison function itself (if it exists in executor.py or rerun_tasks.py), or add an e2e test that: (1) records the original task's file SHA in the handoff record, (2) modifies the file, (3) starts a rerun, (4) asserts the guard detected a mismatch by comparing stored SHA != current SHA. Check that the SHA is actually persisted in the handoff record's produced_artifacts metadata or a dedicated sha256 field.

cross_cutting_observations.title: No tests verify per-task subprocess actually receives the isolated env vars
cross_cutting_observations.why: test_per_task_env_isolation.py verifies execute_phase_tasks populates _env_capture with distinct CLAUDE_SETTINGS_DIR values (assertion 1) and that concurrent workers with distinct settings dirs do not corrupt each other (assertion 2). But it does NOT verify that the env vars from setup_isolation are actually PASSED to the ClaudeProcess subprocess (executor.py:1512, env_vars=_task_env(...)). A bug in _task_env that returns an empty dict would cause per-task subprocesses to inherit the parent env, defeating isolation, but the _env_capture test would still pass because it only checks the captured dict, not what the subprocess received.
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Add a test that uses a real subprocess (not _subprocess_factory stub) which echoes os.environ['CLAUDE_SETTINGS_DIR'] to a file, then asserts the file contains the expected per-task isolated path. Or patch subprocess.Popen to capture the env kwarg and assert it contains the isolation keys. This closes the gap between 'isolation env was computed' and 'isolation env was applied.'

cross_cutting_observations.title: No tests for scheduler.topological_launch_order with complex dependency graphs
cross_cutting_observations.why: scheduler.py:74 (topological_launch_order) groups tasks into dependency waves for bounded parallelism, and raises CycleError on cycles. But tests/sprint/ contains NO dedicated scheduler tests. The only coverage comes indirectly from test_handoff_performance.py, which uses 2-4 independent tasks (no dependencies) or a simple 2-task chain. Complex graphs are not tested: diamond dependencies (A→B, A→C, B→D, C→D should yield waves [[A],[B,C],[D]]), cross-phase dependencies (filtered by dependencies_of), or the CycleError path (A→B→C→A). The scheduler is the correctness foundation for K>1; untested edge cases could cause deadlocks or mis-ordering.
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Add tests/sprint/test_scheduler.py with parametrized tests covering: (1) diamond graph, (2) multi-wave chain, (3) cycle detection (assert CycleError raised with correct unresolved list), (4) self-edges (should be dropped per dependencies_of:58), (5) missing deps (cross-phase, should be filtered out). Verify wave groupings exactly match expected parallelizable sets.

cross_cutting_observations.title: No tests verify HandoffRecord.from_task_result correctly maps all 12 fields
cross_cutting_observations.why: test_handoff_record.py:968 tests HandoffRecord.from_task_result for a happy-path TaskResult, asserting 10 of the 12 fields are correctly derived. But it does NOT test edge cases: (1) a TaskResult with None timestamps (started_at/finished_at), (2) an empty dependencies list, (3) a FAIL_TERMINAL status with GateOutcome.FAIL, (4) the produced_artifacts and consumed_upstreams delta fields being empty lists. The test also does not verify the schema_version defaults to 1 when from_task_result is called (it only checks the default constructor).
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Add parametrized tests for from_task_result covering: FAIL_TERMINAL + GateOutcome.FAIL, INCOMPLETE status, empty dependencies, None timestamps (should serialize as empty string or 'null'), and verify schema_version is always 1. This ensures the factory method is robust to all TaskResult states.

cross_cutting_observations.title: No tests verify rerun-tasks recovery with handoff records
cross_cutting_observations.why: The PR introduces HandoffRecord-based resume (H5), where a task with a validated-success handoff record is skipped on resume. test_e2e_rerun_happy_path.py tests the rerun CLI path end-to-end, but it uses the pre-Stage-1 legacy path (no handoff/ directory or handoff_store). The test verifies task T01.02 is re-run after failure, but does NOT verify that T01.01 and T01.03 (which passed in run 1) are SKIPPED in run 2 because their handoff records mark them validated-success. Without this, the H5 resume skip logic (executor.py:1272-1291) has no e2e coverage.
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Add test_e2e_rerun_with_handoff_skip to test_e2e_rerun_happy_path.py (or a new file) that: (1) runs a 3-task phase with handoff_enabled=True, (2) fails T01.02, (3) starts a rerun with --resume-task T01.02, (4) asserts the control file shows T01.01 and T01.03 were NOT re-run (run count still 1), (5) asserts T01.02 run count is 2. Verify handoff records for T01.01 and T01.03 still exist and were not overwritten.

notes_for_orchestrator: The test suite exercises the new per-task execution paths (subprocess spawn, env isolation, turn counting, handoff records, bounded parallelism) but has 9 high/critical-severity gaps: vacuous concurrency tests (no forced contention), missing atomicity tests (TurnLedger.try_launch), incomplete crash-consistency tests (simulates state but not mid-write interrupt), and missing end-to-end resume coverage (handoff-based skip). The fake_claude harness default (num_turns=0) also masks the regression the Stage-0 wiring is supposed to prevent. Coverage gaps span scheduler.py (no complex dependency graphs), SHA-guard (no hash-comparison verification), and rerun_tasks.py integration with handoff records. Recommend priority: (1) fix fake_claude default to non-zero, (2) add TurnLedger.try_launch contention test, (3) add scheduler unit tests, (4) strengthen concurrency tests with Barrier-aligned starts.
